newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Mobistar in first roaming deal with U.S.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Mobistar in first roaming deal with U.S.

text.p: Belgian mobile phone company Mobistar NV said on Friday it and four other GSM operators signed a deal with U.S. American Personal Communications (APC) to launch transatlantic roaming with the areas of Washington D.C. and Baltimore.
Mobistar said the deal will allow its subscribers to use Sprint Spectrum, the GSM network developed by APC for Washington D.C. and Baltimore, from February 17.
"Mobistar is the first Belgian operator and one of the first five (GSM mobile phone companies) in the world to offer roaming in the United States," it said in a statement.
It said the GSM technology used in Europe (900 Mhz) had so far been incompatible with 1,900 Mhz technology in the U.S.
But APC, the first U.S. GSM operator, and Mobistar's controlling shareholder France Telecom, have set up a conversion system making the two compatible, it said.
It said that Sprint Spectrum would also open up for France Telecom Mobiles, Britain's Cellnet, Hong Kong Telecom CSL and Dutch PTT Telecom.
Mobistar said that its agreement with APC was important because of the presence of numerous international and governmental organisations in Belgium and in Washington.

"Offering roaming with the regions of Washington and Baltimore is the first step towards a larger coverage in the United States...the next step will be New York (Omnipoint)," Mobistar's international roaming manager Serena Romano said in the statement.

Mobistar, Belgium's second GSM network operator, is owned 62 percent by France Telecom. Belgian data communications company Telinfo NV has 10 percent and a group of eight other Belgian investors 28 percent.
It has signed up 68,000 subscribers four months after its launch, 42,000 more than expected.
Belgium's first GSM network Proximus is operated by Belgacom Mobile, itself 75-percent owned by Belgian state telephone operator Belgacom and 25-percent by AirTouch Communications Inc .
